Detailed Description

----
 [[#topofthepage|Big]] class encapsulates the bigfile format and provides a way of accessing the member files.

Member Enumeration Documentation

----
'''enum rw::core::Big::BigfileType'''

This package (tools and libraries) support these types of bigfiles.
'''Enumerator:'''
''BFTYPE_FAST''
Preferred format. 32-byte header, fixed-size index entries with hashed names for fast searching, per-file flags and optional name strings. Compression formats supported: refpack, chunked refpack, and chunked zlib.

Created by the bigfile tool.
''BFTYPE_N''
Legacy format. Each index entry has an N-byte-sized offset and size field, where N can be 2, 3, 4, or 5. Supports bigfiles up to 2^40 bytes in size. Can compress with refpack. Created by the glump tool.
''BFTYPE_24''
Legacy format. Each index entry has a 24-bit offset and size field. The maximum size total size of a bigfile with this type of header is 16MB. Created by the glump tool with the -24 option.
''BFTYPE_HASH16''
Legacy format. Hash16 format (offset/zSize/size/32-bit hash for name) Created by the bighead tool with the -hash16 option.
''BFTYPE_HASH20''
Legacy format. Hash20 format (offset/zSize/size/64-bit hash for name) Created by the bighead tool with the -hash20 option.
''BFTYPE_UNKNOWN''
This is not a recognized type of bigfile.
'''enum rw::core::Big::LocateOptions'''

''LOCATE_OPT_SLASH_CONVERT_FORWARD''
All backslashes will be converted to forward slashes (glump -paths2)

bool rw::core::Big::FindFileByHash(uint64_t hashedName, uint64_t *entryOffset, uint64_t *entrySize, uint64_t *zSize, int *tocIndex, unsigned int *entryFlags) const

Search for a member file by hash value.

This function searches for the given subfile in the header. The header must be in BFTYPE_FAST, BFTYPE_HASH16, or BFTYPE_HASH20 format


'''Parameters:'''
     ''hashedName'' 32-bit DJB2 hash of the name to search for, in big-endian format.
     ''entryoffset'' A 64-bit buffer to receive the offset of the member file. May be NULL. If the file is not found, 0 will be filled in.
     ''entrysize'' A 64-bit buffer to receive the uncompressed size of the member file. May be NULL. If the file is not found, 0 will be filled in.
     ''zipSize'' A 64-bit buffer to receive the compressed size of the member file. May be NULL. If the file is not found, 0 will be filled in.
     ''tocindex'' A pointer to an integer to start the search from. May be NULL. If set and non-zero, the search will start at that record and continue until a matching name is found or until the last record is checked. Records prior to the tocindex will NOT be checked for a matching name. If a match is found, tocindex is updated with that record index. If no match is found, tocindex is set to -1. Basically, this parameter can speed up the linear search by allowing the search to ignore all records, before tocindex.
     ''entryFlags'' A pointer to a unsigned int which receives the per-file flags in fileformat.h. Only applicable to BFTYPE_FAST- format bigfiles.

'''Returns:'''
     true if the file was found, false if not.

'''See also:'''

const char * rw::core::Big::LocateEntry(const char *name, int entryNum, uint64_t *entryOffset, uint64_t *entrySize, void **tocPtr, int *tocIndex, unsigned int flags) const

Locate file in bigfile return size, offset, name.

'''Library:''' rwbigfile

Legacy function supporting BFTYPE_N and BFTYPE_24 formats. Does not work with BFTYPE_HASH16, BFTYPE_HASH20, or BFTYPE_FAST formats.

The LocateEntry function searches a big file directory for the specified file and returns the offset and size of the file. If entryname is not NULL then a case-insensitive search for that file name is performed, otherwise the entrynum-th file in the big file is located. The returned offset is from the start of the bigfile.

Note that the path directory separator character must be consistent with what was used when the bigfile was produced. i.e. If your file path is \"dir\\file.txt\" but the index contains \"dir/file.txt\", the entry will not be found. glump has options to use either forward slahes or back slashes for the paths, and this function takes flags that can also modify the path at runtime to use consistent directory separator characters.


'''Returns:'''
     A pointer to the name of the lump file is returned, or NULL is returned on failure to find the requested file. The offset and size are returned via the pointers entryoffset and entrysize.

'''See also:'''
      [[#classrw_1_1core_1_1_big_1eb7b55657782b09cbb1cd0f25a037668|GetHeaderSize]] , [[#classrw_1_1core_1_1_big_1f1f194eb7652bb7bcc9aefbbb970797c|GetCount]] , [[#classrw_1_1core_1_1_big_1c8d14fa99a45bbc5ca4330656cefdd0e|GetHeaderType]] , [[#classrw_1_1core_1_1_big_110d7fa87150094c2ee030216891b2465|FindFileByName]] , [[#classrw_1_1core_1_1_big_1d0baa904810457bf809bacc61f171a15|FindFileByHash]] , [[#classrw_1_1core_1_1_big_14f5d9aa5dd508a5138427441e6ebc185|FindFileByIndex]] , [[#classrw_1_1core_1_1_big_1bd45307b54ba9f9be8cde4da53539235|FindNameByIndex]]

Detailed Description

----
This class implements a file system handler for Bigfiles.

After the object has been registered with the file library, use [[#classrw_1_1core_1_1_big_handler_1f17b6210589c35efd320348925a1f6b7|BigHandler::AddArchiveFromFile]] to register one or more bigfiles with the device. Files inside bigfiles can then be loaded as if they were on the normal file system.

This class supports directory searches, but if you use that feature, the name strings must be available, otherwise no patterns will match.

'''enum rw::core::BigHandler::AddOption'''

Flags for AddArchiveFromFile.
'''Enumerator:'''
''ADDFLAG_USE_ALTERNATE_HEADER''
Use an alternate header instead of the one included in the bigfile. The name should be \".bh\". If the alternate header is not available, the header inside the main bigfile will be used as a fallback.
''ADDFLAG_ADD_TO_HEAD''
Add the big file to the handler as head. The newly added big file will be searched first.
''ADDFLAG_DRM''
When opening the bigfile (and the alternate header, if used), append the .edat extension and pass the AsyncOp::FOPEN_DRM flag when the bigfile (but not the subfiles) are opened. You must be using rwfilesystem 1.07.00 or later for this flag to be respected. If not, this flag is silently ignored.
''ADDFLAG_SLASH_CONVERT_FORWARD''
This option will convert any backslashes in the path provided by the caller to forward slashes before doing the name lookup. Use this if you built your bigfiles with the paths2 option.
''ADDFLAG_SLASH_CONVERT_BACKWARD''
This option will convert any forward slashes in the path provided by the caller to backslashes before doing the name lookup. Use this if you built your bigfiles with the paths4 option.
''ADDFLAG_NAME_CONVERT_LOWERCASE''
This option will convert names provided by the caller to lowercase before doing the name lookup. See -tolower in glump.exe or -nameLower in bigfile.exe
''ADDFLAG_NAME_CONVERT_UPPERCASE''
This option will convert names provided by the caller to uppercase before doing the name lookup. See -toupper in glump.exe or -nameUpper in bigfile.exe
''ADDFLAG_EXTERNAL_DECOMPRESS''
Use this flag to decompress external to rwbigfile, ie. ignore BIGFILE_FORMAT_FLAG_COMPRESSION_TYPE_*.
''ADDFLAG_LOAD_NAME_INDEX''
This flag tells the handler to load the name index. The use-case for loading the name index is to do wild-card searches.
''ADDFLAG_ADD_PERMANENT_HEAD''
Add the big file to the handler as a permanent head. The newly added big file will always be searched first. Example use would be for a patch.big file where patched data should always take precedence over other files.
''ADDFLAG_FILE_USES_SDATA''
'''enum rw::core::BigHandler::OpenFlags'''

Flags for Open.
'''Enumerator:'''
''FOPEN_DECOMPRESS_IN_PLACE''
Use in-place decompression, if the output buffer is large enough. This feature avoids the need for a temporary buffer to hold the compressed data. Instead, the compressed data is read into the tail end of the output buffer, and decompressed to the start. Requires that the buffer be a few bytes larger than the decompressed file size. If this flag is not specified, or the buffer is not large enough to hold the file, the decompression will be done via streaming, which is not as fast and requires temporary buffers.

rwbigfile library ChangeLog



============================================================================== Version 1.05.02

Changes.
  • Support for rwstdc has been removed.


  • Critical sections added in parts of the bigfile handler to improve thread safety.


  • A flag was added to the bigfile handler to indicate that it should not decompress data automatically but pass it compressed back to the user.


  • The bigfile tool has added -toUpper and -toLower command line options.


  • The bigfile tool now does not sort the index by default but includes files in the order they are specified on the command line or via response file, to maintain compatibility with Glump's conventions.


  • A "permanent head" file has been added to the handler that lets the user specify a big file that will always remain at the head of the list and, hence, will always be searched first.


  • Support for in-memory big files has been added.


  • The bigfile handler now can pass through the appropriate SDATA flag to the underlying PS3 rwfilesystem driver.


  • The bigfile tool has been ported to Linux and OS X.


Version 1.05.01 - (March 3, 2010)

New features.
  • Bigfile has the added ability to merge big file archives.
  • Files contained in a big file can now be opened via their index. For example:

              AsyncOp op;
              op.Open("big:mybigfile.big,5"); // Opens the fifth file in mybigfile.big
  • Bigfile allows files to be serialized into the archive in either the order they are specified on the command line or alphabetically.
  • Bigfile allows the index to be sorted by file offset which is required for consistent behavior with the index lookup feature mentioned above.


Changes.
  • WinBig was updated to read new big file formats, including those whose contents have been packed using the new chunk compression formats.


Bug fixes. The following bugs have been fixed in this release:
  • Avoid reading the next chunk info if we have read the last chunk which was causing crashes when the chunk abuts unrelated data.
  • WinBig would crash when opening files created with the -fat option.
  • Bigfile would not extract files from a big file archive that were compressed.


Version 1.05.00 - (December 11, 2009)

New features. The following features have been added in this release:

  • ETCR-240. A command line option, -compressThreshold, analogous to glump's -packthresh was added to the bigfile tool to specify the minimum size of a file to be compressed.


  • ETCR-243. A feature was added to the bigfile tool allow file names within the big file archive to be specified. The format, sourcefilename=destinationfilename, follows glump's convention and an additional command line parameter, -sourcefile, was introduced to disable this renaming.


  • ETCR-244. The bigfile tool returns a non-zero result when a failure occurs.


  • ETCR-245. The bigfile tool has the ability to sort alphabetically, analagous to glump's -sort3 option.


  • A new constructor has been added to the Big class that takes an option indicating whether or not it should load the name index automatically. This only works with new-style big files.


  • A new method, GetBaseAddress(), has been added to the Big class to fetch the base address of the bigfile data in memory.


Bug fixes. The following bugs have been fixed in this release:

  • ETCR-238. Wildcards searches in big files were greedily matching subdirectories causing unexpected and inconsistent behavior with other file system components.


  • ETCR-259. Files previously could have been compressed using the bigfile tool using LZX but the runtime would not be able to read them.


  • Loading an old-format bigfile after a new-format bigfile would cause reads of files from the old-format file to fail.


Version 1.04.00 - (September 30, 2009)

Changes. The following API changes have been made in this release:

  • the glump and bighead tools are deprecated. They have been superceded by a new tool called "bigfile", which authors bigfiles using a format similar to what bighead uses. Refer to the documentation included in the tool for how to use it. The bigfile tool is basically a stripped-down glump. If there are features in glump that would prevent you from using the bigfile tool, please let us know at and we'll add them back in after the use case is understood.


New features. The following features have been added in this release:

  • ETCR-106. If you're using rwfilesystem 1.12.00 or later, the bigfile handler will spawn another thread to decompress the data. This can result in improved performance on data being read from the hard drive because the next read can start while the current one is still decompressing. You don't need to take any special action to enable this feature, it will be automatically enabled if you build rwbigfile with rwfilesystem 1.12.00 or later.


  • ETCR-149. It is now possible to search other bigfiles if the file you requested wasn't found in the bigfile specified. Pass the flag [[RWCore:RWBigfile:API:rw::core::BigHandler#classrw_1_1core_1_1_big_handler_1a71691d9dfaba0a9d063a679a8c703e436476815a67bf96d985662c8f14d69b5|rw::core::BigHandler::FOPEN_SEARCH_OTHER_BIGFILES]] to the AsyncOp::Open function. If the file is located in the specified bigfile, that file is returned.. If the file is not located in the specified bigfile, all other bigfiles will be searched and the first match will be returned.


  • ETCR-150. Wildcarded file names can be used with the HASH16 index format. In order to do this, the name index must be loaded in addition to the hashed index. This feature is only available in BFTYPE_FAST bigfiles, which must be created with the new bigfile tool. The header rw/core/bigfile/fileformat.h describe the new format. Three new functions have been added to the runtime library, [[RWCore:RWBigfile:API:rw::core::Big#classrw_1_1core_1_1_big_134c3f3c9f5f00e5fc5c7632e0b4a0364|rw::core::Big::GetNameIndexSize()]] , [[RWCore:RWBigfile:API:rw::core::Big#classrw_1_1core_1_1_big_17ec0850532059de20d11a953696d2a7f|rw::core::Big::SetNameIndex()]] , and [[RWCore:RWBigfile:API:rw::core::Big#classrw_1_1core_1_1_big_1bd45307b54ba9f9be8cde4da53539235|rw::core::Big::FindNameByIndex()]] . Pass the flag [[RWCore:RWBigfile:API:rw::core::BigHandler#classrw_1_1core_1_1_big_handler_1b3c04cf892a0a93ba958799d8da3fdd6d6b20322c490d1387083edae02c9a4e6|rw::core::BigHandler::ADDFLAG_LOAD_NAME_INDEX]] to AddArchiveFromFile if you want to be able to perform wildcard searches on the loaded bigfile. The runtime library continues to handle all formats (new bigfile, legacy bigfile, and bighead) for now. At some point in the future, support for the legacy formats may be removed, and they are generally inefficient so we encourage you to migrate your toolchain to the bigfile tool.


  • ETCR-226. The bigfile tool and runtime library support chunked asset decompression. rwcodec-1.04.00 or later is required to use this feature. Set a decompression job with rw::core::BigHandler::SetDecompressJobInfo().


Bug fixes. The following bugs have been fixed in this release:

  • ETCR-118. When extracting files from a bigfile using the glump tool, if the file was in a non-existent subdirectory, it was skipped. This bug has been fixed.


Version 1.03.00 - (September 11, 2008)

  • Links to release notes for this and older versions are available on the package server.
